story.content: The first sip is cold as a moonbeam and warm as a story told in the dark. It tastes like sugar, bells, and the tiny thrill of stepping where the rules do not quite apply.
“Begin at the beginning,” the hourglass murmured, “and go on until you come to the end; then stop.”

story.caption: The drink glitters like a pocket mirror under lantern light.

story.content: This one spins the room a little sideways. It is bright and insistent, with the weight of a card game played after midnight.

story.caption: A drifting tea-tray under the moon.

story.content: “It’s no use going back to yesterday,” said Alice, “because I was a different person then.”
The color of a rose in candlelight and the bite of a good dare. It leaves a little warmth behind the teeth and a little wonder in the shoulders.
“The question is,” said Alice, “whether you can make words mean so many different things.”
A bittersweet little spell with the hush of a dusty attic and the sparkle of a sudden clue. It feels like standing in a doorway while the world tilts just a fraction.

story.caption: The last candle burns under the snow-lost mountain.

story.content: “A little room with a table and a tea-tray in it.”

story.caption: The glass hums like a song in the dark.
